title: Learning to Generate Stylized Handwritten Text via a Unified Representation of Style, Content, and Noise
claim: Prior methods need separate style and content encoders plus extra losses; ours feeds everything to one diffusion model with a single loss.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed dividers, loss equation above each panel
description: A three-panel horizontal comparison of handwritten text-line generation architectures, with dashed vertical lines between the panels. Panel (a), One-DM, has a pink Diffusion Model block with a noise image on top. To its right sit a Style Encoder, a Content Encoder and a Fusion Module in peach, and the handwriting inputs feed into these. Its loss is L_diff + L_lapNCE + L_CTC. Panel (b), TGC-Diff, has a green Diffusion Model block, a single peach Style Encoder, and a content line added to the noise with a ⊕ symbol. Its loss is L_diff + L_high-freq. Panel (c), Ours, has a stack of noise and handwriting text-line images feeding directly into one blue rounded Diffusion Model block. This outputs multi-line handwriting, and the loss is just L_diff. Panels (a) and (b) are visibly more complex than (c), which is the simplest.
caption: Structural comparison of handwritten text-line generation methods. Unlike previous approaches, our model integrates style and content modeling without additional encoders, yielding a streamlined architecture.
abstract: Handwritten Text Generation (HTG) seeks to synthesize realistic and personalized handwriting by modeling stylistic and structural traits. While recent diffusion-based approaches have advanced generation fidelity, they typically rely on auxiliary style or content encoders with handcrafted objectives, leading to complex training pipelines and limited interaction across factors. In this work, we present InkSpire, a diffusion transformer based model that unifies style, content, and noise within a shared latent space. By eliminating explicit encoders, InkSpire streamlines optimization while enabling richer feature interaction and stronger in-context generation. To further enhance flexibility, we introduce a multi-line masked infilling strategy that allows training directly on raw text-line images, together with a revised positional encoding that supports arbitrary-length multi-line synthesis and fine-grained character editing. Moreover, InkSpire is trained on a bilingual Chinese–English corpus, enabling a single model to handle both Chinese and English handwriting generation with high fidelity and stylistic diversity, thereby overcoming the need for language-specific systems. Extensive experiments on IAM and ICDAR2013 demonstrate that InkSpire achieves superior structural accuracy and stylistic diversity compared to prior state-of-the-art methods.
